name: Filesystem MCP Server
what: Reference MCP server that lets an AI read, write, edit, move and search files and directories, restricted to the folders you pass it. Version 2.0.1 (25 Oct 2026) includes security fixes for how it checks paths.
who: People who want Claude Desktop or another chat app to work with files on their computer.

setup.text: Install Node.js 24 or later. Version 2.0.0 raised the minimum from earlier Node versions to 24, and the README says the server needs Node 24+ when it runs through npx.
Add the server to your MCP client config, listing each folder the AI may access as an argument (at least one is required):
On Windows, the README launches npx through cmd /c:

Only list folders you're happy for the AI to access. Folders passed on the command line work with every protocol version. MCP Roots, where a client sets the folders for you, only works with older (2025-era) clients and is deprecated; 2026-07-28 clients can't use it. With no folders on the command line, the server exits at startup if a 2025-era client doesn't support Roots, and answers every tool call with an error for a 2026-07-28 client. Restart the client after editing its config.

Already running a date-versioned release (2025.x or 2026.x)? The project warns that package managers rank 2.0.1 below those, so they won't offer it as an upgrade. Install it explicitly, or pin it in your config:

install.name: filesystem
notes: Replace the path with a folder the AI may access. You can list more folders; at least one is required.

prompts: Find every markdown file in my notes folder that mentions 'invoice'.
Show me a directory tree of my project folder, excluding node_modules.
Read my README and suggest a clearer intro, then preview the edit before applying it.
